title: Post-incident privacy preservation notice and customer guidance
content:
TL;DR:
We experienced a service incident that temporarily exposed some internal request metadata in logs for a subset of tenant inference traffic. No customer application payloads were persisted in an analyzable form that could reveal end-user content, and we have completed a scoped privacy-preservation workflow: affected logs were identified, snapshots were cryptographically hashed and sealed, raw artifacts were securely deleted where not required for regulatory retention, and an auditable evidence bundle is available to enterprise customers on request.

Purpose of this doc:
- Draft customer-facing notice focusing on privacy/data-handling after the incident.
- Intended for account teams to include with a technical statuspage update or postmortem packet.
- Not legal clearance — please route to Legal for final signoff before sending to regulated customers.

1) What happened (plain language):
- On 2026-07-06 at ~03:14 UTC a routing misconfiguration caused an internal debug pipeline to capture a small slice of request metadata (headers, routing IDs, sampling traces) for 0.04% of requests routed to the eu-west inference cluster.
- The pipeline briefly persisted the metadata in internal temporary logs before the error was detected and the pipeline was disabled.
- Importantly: we did not persist inference input or output payloads in an indexable/plaintext form. Payloads were present only as encrypted KV blobs tied to a transient cache and were not exported to analytics systems.

2) What types of data were in the temporary logs:
- Request timestamps, routing identifiers, and truncated IP prefixes (e.g., 203.0.113.0/24).
- Service-level headers (model variant, tenant-id, region, sampling flags).
- No full user messages, no customer-supplied files, and no plaintext embeddings were present in the preserved logs we examined.

3) How we verified and contained the exposure:
- Immediate actions (within 30 minutes): disabled the debug capture pipeline; blocked the relevant routing rule; revoked temporary service credentials used by the pipeline.
- Forensics: created a narrow query to identify all affected log fragments; every fragment was exported into a sealed evidence bundle and cryptographically hashed (SHA-256) with a timestamped manifest.
- Privacy-preservation steps: any fragment containing even partial payload-like content was redacted and retained only in hashed form for the audit bundle. Where retention was not required, raw fragments were securely deleted using the standard secure-delete workflow (WORM-backed deletion + deletion confirmation events).

4) What we are doing for customers now:
- Evidence bundle: an auditable, time-stamped evidence bundle (manifest + SHA-256 checksums) is available to enterprise customers upon request. The bundle includes a small searchable index that only surfaces metadata tags (tenant id, time range, hash) and never raw payload content.
- Optional verification: customers who need independent verification can request temporary, read-only access to the hashed manifest and deletion proofs; access is granted under an NDA or existing Data Processing Agreement (DPA) terms.
- Proactive mitigations: applied orthogonal config gating so debug capture pipelines require two independent config flags; added a pre-deploy lint that catches routing rules that would leak internal debug sinks to production clusters.
- Longer-term changes: rolling out strict sampling controls, auto-redaction heuristics in debug pipelines, and a new alert if any capture pipeline logs contain >16 bytes of non-header data.

5) What this means for your application and users:
- If you are an enterprise customer with higher regulatory needs (e.g., healthcare, finance), we recommend you request the evidence bundle and deletion proofs so your audit/compliance teams can verify.
- No action required for most customers. If you believe your tenant had abnormal traffic patterns during the 03:10–03:40 UTC window, contact your account lead for a targeted verification.

6) FAQ (draft snippets for customer comms):
Q: Were my users' messages exposed?
A: Based on our analysis, plaintext user messages or uploaded files were not persisted in an accessible form. Where questionable fragments existed we redacted them before retention, and the redaction proofs are part of the evidence bundle.

Q: How many customers were affected?
A: Approximately 0.04% of requests routed through the eu-west cluster during the 03:10–03:40 UTC window. We have tenant-scoped manifests enabling per-customer verification.

Q: Will Redwood notify end users?
A: We will notify customer accounts. Customers should follow their internal policies for end-user notification; if you require Redwood assistance (templates, evidence extracts) we will provide them under your DPA.

Q: What if my legal or security team wants deeper access?
A: We support licensed evidence review: options include (1) sealed manifest + checksums, (2) redacted artifact review with an on-site/virtual signing session, or (3) hashed-only proof with third-party auditor attestation. Reach out to your account rep to coordinate.

7) Suggested short statuspage blurb (for ops to copy/paste):
"Privacy update: A transient debug capture stored limited request metadata for a small subset of requests in eu-west on 2026-07-06. No plaintext customer messages were exposed. We have sealed and audited the artifacts, deleted unnecessary raw fragments, and made an evidence bundle available to affected enterprise customers."

8) Suggested enterprise email subject lines (pick one):
- "Redwood privacy-preservation notice — limited debug-log exposure (2026-07-06)"
- "Actionable evidence bundle available — limited routing debug capture"

9) Suggested attachment list for customer packet:
- Short timeline (10–12 lines)
- Redacted evidence manifest (hashes + per-tenant index)
- Deletion confirmation summary (dates + internal ticket ids)
- Contact card (account rep + security liaison)

10) Internal notes for Legal/Compliance reviewers (do not include in customer packet):
- Confirm whether retention of the sealed raw artifacts for 90 days is permissible under active investigations vs customer-requested evidence review.
- Confirm template NDA language for granting read-only verification access to customers.
- Consider offering an optional third-party attestation for large enterprise customers seeking additional assurance.

Next steps (owner: Maya Chen):
- 2026-07-09: Circulate to Legal for wording signoff and confirm retention window.
- 2026-07-10: Prepare packet attachments (manifest, deletion proof) for account teams.
- 2026-07-12: Publish statuspage blurb and send tailored notices to affected accounts after Legal signoff.

Notes to self / scratch:
- Keep language plain and avoid technical absolutes e.g., use "based on our analysis" rather than "definitely not".
- Coordinate with SRE to add the two-flag gating to the debug pipeline PR (infra repo PR-1227).
- Draft customer templates for data-protection officers (1-page) — include sample wording for GDPR/CCPA triggers.
